title: Tierwise compile case expected.yaml
description: The expected.yaml of one compile case (spec section 12.5). It states either the bundle file that the compile must produce, or the complete list of findings. A findings entry is a finding key (code, file, path, line) and carries no severity, message or suggestion ([VEC-97], [FIND-24]). This schema checks structure only. Semantic checks, such as that bundle names a file in bundles/, that codes are engine codes or lint rules, and that finding keys are compared as sets, are done by the runner and the check tool.

id.description: Case identifier. It equals the name of the case directory directly under compile/ ([VEC-13]).

specVersion.description: Version of this specification that the case targets. The value for this version is "0.1" ([VEC-14]).

clauses.description: Clause IDs that define the behaviour the case checks ([VEC-16]).

description.description: One non-empty, single-line sentence that says what the case checks ([VEC-17]).

project.description: Relative path, from the directory of this file, to a sample project directory inside the repository's samples/ directory. The case then compiles that sample in place, and the case has no project/ directory ([VEC-91]). Omitted when the case has its own project/ directory ([VEC-5]). The pattern checks only that the path is relative, uses / and has a samples/ segment followed by at least one more segment. The runner checks that it resolves to a directory in the repository's samples/ directory.

build.description: Optional build record that the runner passes to the provenance writer ([VEC-107]). It affects only the sidecar, never the bundle bytes ([DET-3]). Each member is optional.

expect.description: The expected outcome. It has exactly one of two members: bundle, or findings ([VEC-90]).

clauseId.description: A clause ID: an area prefix from spec.md, a hyphen and a number from 1 ([VEC-16]).

build.description: Build members for the sidecar. Each value takes the form that [BUNDLE-150] gives. Any other member is a runner failure ([VEC-107], [VEC-19]).

gitCommit.description: Full commit identifier: 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. Quote it, so that YAML does not read an all-digit value as a number ([BUNDLE-150]).

createdAt.description: RFC 3339 time in UTC, with an uppercase T separator, a Z offset, and seconds without fractional seconds ([BUNDLE-150], [BUNDLE-141]).

publisher.description: Opaque label that names the publisher ([BUNDLE-150], [BUNDLE-142]).

expect.description: Exactly one of bundle or findings ([VEC-90]).

oneOf.description: A bundle expectation: the compile produces no finding of any severity, and its output bytes equal the named bundle file ([VEC-94], [DET-1]).

bundle.description: Relative path, from the directory of this file, to a canonical bundle file directly inside bundles/ and not inside bundles/invalid/ ([VEC-93], [VEC-9]). The pattern checks only that the path is relative, uses / and ends in bundles/ followed by one file name, which excludes bundles/invalid/. The runner checks that the path resolves to the suite's bundles/ directory.

oneOf.description: A findings expectation: the complete set of finding keys that the compiler reports, of every severity ([VEC-95], [VEC-98]).

findings.description: A non-empty list in which no two entries are equal ([VEC-96]).

finding.description: One expected finding key: (code, file, path, line) ([VEC-97], [FIND-24]). Messages, suggestions and severities are not compared ([VEC-101]).

code.description: An engine error code of requirements 6.1 (the engine errors of spec/error-codes.md), or a lint rule identifier of [LINT-1]: one of the fixed identifiers, or naming/<name> for a naming pattern, where <name> is non-empty and has no /, * or white space ([LINT-14]). The evaluation-only codes of requirements 6.2 and E_PROVENANCE_INVALID are not finding codes. Codes are compared exactly ([VEC-99], [VEC-100]).

anyOf.description: An engine error code of requirements 6.1 ([FIND-12]).
A fixed lint rule identifier of [LINT-1] ([FIND-13]).
A naming rule naming/<name>, one for each naming pattern ([LINT-12], [LINT-14]).

file.description: Source path relative to the project root, with / as the separator ([VEC-102], [FIND-17]).

path.description: The path to the node that the finding names, as a list ([VEC-104], [FIND-20]). A string item is a mapping key, compared by exact code point. A non-negative integer item is a zero-based sequence index. The root is the empty list. Example: [features, "a.b", rules, 1].

line.description: The 1-based line of the finding ([VEC-103], [FIND-21]). A duplicate key is reported at its second occurrence ([SRC-9]).
